LESSON: SIMPLE EQUATIONS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.8: Simple Equations

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Simple Equations. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. form simple equations with one unknown involving real- life situations
2. solve simple equations with one unknown involving real- life situations
3. appreciate use of equations in solving problems in real life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: SIMPLE EQUATIONS
Simple Equations is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Simple Equations problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Simple Equations question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Simple Equations question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Simple Equations set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Simple Equations.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Simple Equations in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. form simple equations with one unknown involving real- life situations
2. solve simple equations with one unknown involving real- life situations
3. appreciate use of equations in solving problems in real life

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
